In this study, we select Mistral-7B (Jiang et al., 2023) as our base model for domain-adaptive continual pre-training. We perform continual pretraining using DeepSpeed (Rasley et al., 2020) with its ZeRO stage-1 optimizer, setting the batch size to 1M tokens and utilizing bf16 precision. We adopt a Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning rate scheduler (Hu et al., 2024) with a maximum learning rate of 2e-5, involving a $3\%$ warm-up phase and an exponential decay phase during the last $10\%$ of the training process.

During fine-tuning, we train all the models on downstream tasks for 5 epochs, using a cosine learning rate schedule with a maximum rate of 5e-6 and a $3\%$ warm-up phase. For both few-shot and fine-tuned settings, we use vLLM (0.4.2) (Kwon et al., 2023) to accelerate inference.

For the in-domain corpus in ads domain, after extracting text from webpages, we filter them through the following four processes:

1. Filtering search ad samples containing personally identifiable information (PII) using a rule-based filter (e.g., checking for email addresses or phone numbers).   
2. Filtering out non-English samples and those with low English classifier scores using a fastText-based language identifier. These latter samples often contain a large number of meaningless symbols.   
3. Filtering samples that are either too long or too short, as these samples often contain noisy texts.   
4. Filtering samples where all words start with a certain symbol (e.g., +, #) using a Regular Expression-based refiner.

These rule-based filters are defined by observing the initial retrieved ad samples and should be adapted according to the data from different domains. Note that we do not further filter the retrieved math samples, which originate from the MathPile (Wang et al., 2023) and Proof-Pile-2 (Azerbayev et al., 2023) corpora and have already been strictly filtered.
